title: Set up your sound
summary: Choose the microphone and the call audio Overtalk listens to.

steps.title: Pick your microphone
steps.body: Open the recorder and choose your microphone. Your choice is remembered for future recordings.

steps.title: Pick the call audio
steps.body: Choose the system-audio source in the recorder so the other people on the call are recorded too.

steps.title: Check the levels
steps.body: Use Run setup check on Home. Record a 10-second sound check while speaking and playing call audio, listen to it, then confirm both sources are audible. Check model readiness before finishing setup.

tips: Wearing headphones keeps your microphone from picking up the call twice.

title: Know your way around
summary: One screen holds everything: your meetings, the timeline, the transcript and the selected moment.

steps.title: Meetings
steps.body: Recordings and imports land here. Search, pin, archive and sort your meetings; waveform previews are optional.

steps.title: Transport
steps.body: Record, play and stop, the clock, and the meeting title. Click the title to rename it.

steps.title: Lanes
steps.body: The timeline opens with the meeting. Auto fit shows its lanes using the available height; hide it when you want more room to read.

steps.title: Transcript
steps.body: Select a passage to inspect it. Play from starts at its timestamp; Edit lets you correct the words and speaker.

steps.title: Inspector
steps.body: Whatever you select appears here, with Play from and Copy.

title: Record a meeting
summary: Press record before the call starts; Overtalk transcribes as people speak.

steps.title: Press record
steps.body: Connect Google or Microsoft to see Coming up on Home. Join & take notes opens the meeting link in its normal app and begins a named recording. You can also record a spontaneous conversation.

steps.title: Watch the clock
steps.body: The clock runs while you record. Pause keeps everything so far; stop saves the meeting.

steps.title: Name it
steps.body: Type a title now or later. Untitled recordings are named by date and time.

steps.title: Keep your own notes
steps.body: My notes stays available during the call. Personal writing saves separately. With automatic notes enabled, stopping queues any needed transcription and then generates notes, even after navigation or a restart.

tips: Recording keeps going if you open another meeting. Choose Recording in the header to return to it.
keys: Space plays or pauses a saved meeting

title: Mark moments while you talk
summary: Save a timestamp when something matters, then return to it after the call.

steps.title: Mark the moment
steps.body: Choose Mark moment on the timeline to save the current playback or recording position.

steps.title: Name it if you like
steps.body: Give the bookmark a short name, such as “Budget agreed”, then save it.

steps.title: Find it later
steps.body: Bookmarks appear as pins on the timeline. Open a pin and choose Jump to this moment to return to it.

title: Read a meeting at a glance
summary: See who spoke when, where people talked over each other, and what was decided.

steps.title: Move through the recording
steps.body: Click a speaker lane at the time you want to hear. Use the playback controls to play, pause or move ten seconds at a time.

steps.title: Read the clips
steps.body: Each clip is one stretch of speech, drawn from the recording. Overlapping clips are people talking at once.

steps.title: Follow the transcript
steps.body: Enable Follow playback to keep the current passage visible. Scrolling pauses following until you enable it again.

keys: Space plays or pauses outside a text field
tips: The moving word highlight is a reading aid estimated from passage timestamps. It is not word-level forced alignment; pauses, overlap and mixed languages may drift.

title: Jump to a decision
summary: Decisions and actions from your notes are placed at the moment they were said.

steps.title: Click a decision
steps.body: Amber clips are decisions; violet clips are actions. Select a clip to inspect it. A grouped clip opens all the nearby moments.

steps.title: Read it in full
steps.body: The inspector separates the generated interpretation from the original transcript evidence.

steps.title: Hear it
steps.body: Play from starts the recording at that moment, so you can check the exact words.

tips: A decision only gets a clip when the notes point to a line of the transcript. Regenerate notes after editing the transcript.

title: Listen to one person
summary: Play only one speaker, or skip someone, without changing the recording.

steps.title: Select a speaker lane
steps.body: Click a speaker name on the timeline to reveal Only and Skip. Active playback filters remain visible.

steps.title: Solo
steps.body: Only plays that speaker and skips the silence between their turns.

steps.title: Mute
steps.body: Skip skips that speaker unless someone else is talking over them.

title: Name the speakers
summary: Give voices real names, merge duplicates, or analyse the recording again.

steps.title: Open Speakers
steps.body: The Speakers tab sits next to Transcript.

steps.title: Rename or merge
steps.body: Rename a speaker for this meeting, or merge two labels that are the same person.

steps.title: Improve the transcript
steps.body: Open Meeting details for Analyse recording. It saves a recovery copy before transcribing again.

title: Write notes
summary: Turn the transcript into notes with decisions and actions you can edit.

steps.title: Open the notes
steps.body: The Notes tab opens the notes for this meeting.

steps.title: Generate
steps.body: Automatic notes starts after a recording when enabled. You can also choose Generate notes; Options contains the language, template and model. Processing status and Retry appear above the document.

steps.title: Edit freely
steps.body: Your edits save automatically. A local draft protects changes while saving; Copy notes puts them on the clipboard.

tips: Open Ask beside the notes for My notes, meeting-scoped questions and an editable follow-up draft. Personal notes guide emphasis but do not count as transcript evidence. Review source passages before sharing.

title: Export and share
summary: Save notes and transcript as Markdown, Word, PDF, text or JSON.

steps.title: Export
steps.body: Choose Export above the timeline, select a format, then choose where to save the meeting.

steps.title: Copy a moment
steps.body: Select a passage and choose Copy in the inspector to copy its text. Copy transcript copies the full transcript.

steps.title: Send notes to your tools
steps.body: Choose Send in Notes, select a connected account and destination, then review the content before publishing. Add accounts in Projects → Connections. Some providers need Overtalk’s publisher registration before account sign-in is available.

title: Search your meetings
summary: Find a meeting by its title or by anything said in it.

steps.title: Open search
steps.body: Press Ctrl+K to open the library, or choose Library in the sidebar.

steps.title: Type a word
steps.body: Search for a title or words from a transcript. Open a result to return to the source passage.

title: Ask across meetings
summary: Ask a question and get an answer that quotes the lines it came from.

steps.title: Open the library
steps.body: Choose Library above the meeting list.

steps.title: Build the index once
steps.body: Exact text search works immediately. Library settings can add a local semantic index for searching by meaning.

steps.title: Search or ask
steps.body: Search finds passages; Ask writes an answer with citations. In a meeting, Notes → Ask limits questions to that meeting and can prepare a source-backed follow-up. Drafts stay local until you copy and send them.

title: What stays on this computer
summary: Recordings, transcripts and notes are stored locally. Cloud AI is used only when you choose a cloud provider.

steps.title: Local by default
steps.body: Speech recognition and the default notes model run on this computer.

steps.title: Your choice of model
steps.body: In Summary you can choose a cloud provider instead; meeting text is then sent to it.

steps.title: Where files live
steps.body: General shows the recordings folder. Move meetings to Trash from their menu, then restore or permanently delete them in Trash.
